title: Incorrect Current/Wattage Parsing and Unread Cycle Counts on Samsung Galaxy A15 5G (MediaTek Dimensity 6100+)
body_excerpt: On the Samsung Galaxy A15 5G running One UI, Amply reads charging current as 0W (or 1mA), and charge cycles are not displayed. Inspection via dumpsys battery reveals that the device's MediaTek power management driver outputs current now directly as a 3-digit milliamp integer (441) rather than standard microamps muA, e.g., 441000). Because the app assumes microamps, dividing 441 by 1,000,000 results in approx 0.0004A, which rounds down to 0W. Additionally, total cycle usage is logged under Samsung's custom MediaTek key mSavedBatteryUsage: [54327] (representing 543.27\% accumulated usage / ~543 cycles) instead of the standard Android HAL cycle_count integer, causing cycle reporting to fail. Please add MediaTek unit scaling (mA vs muA) and mSavedBatteryUsage fallback parsing for this device model.

title: Crash: recording waveform races on AudioCaptureManager energy history
body_excerpt: ## Root cause Physical Pixel gate on integrated `develop` commit `6138ef5` reproduced a main-thread crash while recording. `AudioCaptureManager.energyHistory` is an unsynchronized `ArrayDeque`: the capture coroutine mutates it while the timer/main path calls `getEnergyHistory().toList()`. A racing snapshot can expose a transient null backing-array slot, which Kotlin then unboxes in `WaveformBars` and crashes. ## Physical evidence - Pixel 4 (`flame`), Android 15/API 35, ARM64, serial `99071FFAZ00EBN` - exact APK SHA-256: `83be3a08102df9c233493517b6ce9497a3145824ebbee905c4c475b1a3324a17` - microphone capture and foreground service started correctly - crash: `java.lang.NullPointerException` at `WaveformBars.kt:64`, observed while the capture coroutine was updating waveform history - no audio or transcript retained ## Acceptance criteria - Synchronize all reads and writes of the rolling energy history without changing waveform behavior. - Add a deterministic concurrent read/write regression test that fails on the old implementation. - Run targeted tests, all JVM tests, lint, and assemble. - Prove the regression test bites via sabotage/revert. - Independent fresh-context review and exact-head Pixel recording smoke with no crash/ANR. ## Scope/risk Small thread-safety repair; no persisted-state/API/migration changes. Rollback is a single commit. Tracked by #33.

title: `wasmJs` artifact missing from Maven Central — `Unresolved reference 'ismoy'` when compiling for wasmJs target
body_excerpt: When using `imagepickerkmp` in a Kotlin Multiplatform project that includes a `wasmJs` target, compilation fails with `Unresolved reference 'ismoy'` errors for all classes from the library (`rememberImagePickerKMP`, `ImagePickerKMPConfig`, `GalleryConfig`, `ImagePickerResult`, `PhotoResult`). The library is declared in `commonMain.dependencies`, which works correctly for Android, iOS, and Desktop targets. However, the `wasmJs` target fails to compile because the `imagepickerkmp-wasm-js` artifact does not appear to be published to Maven Central. The README and release notes (including 1.0.35) advertise WASM support, but only the following artifacts are available on Maven Central: - `imagepickerkmp-android` - `imagepickerkmp-iosarm64` - `imagepickerkmp-iossimulatorarm64` - `imagepickerkmp-js` - `imagepickerkmp-jvm` There is no `imagepickerkmp-wasm-js` artifact published. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a KMP project with `wasmJs { browser(); binaries.executable() }` target 2. Add `implementation("io.github.ismoy:imagepickerkmp:1.0.41")` to `commonMain.dependencies` 3. title: Linux V8-mode libraries are not linked against libm — `undefined symbol: exp2` on OpenJ9
body_excerpt: ## Summary Since v5.0.0, `libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64.v.*.so` is built without a link to `libm`. It leaves 12 math symbols undefined (`exp2`, `log2`, `pow`, `nan`, `nearbyint`, among others) and relies on the host process to already provide them. That assumption holds on HotSpot, whose `libjvm.so` links `libm.so.6` and is loaded into the global symbol scope, so the undefined symbols quietly bind. It does not hold on Eclipse OpenJ9 / IBM Semeru: their `libjvm.so` links only `libdl`, `libpthread` and `libc`, so nothing fills the gap and the process aborts on the first call. Because the dynamic linker resolves these lazily, the failure surfaces only when one of those symbols is first called, which in practice is V8 teardown at JVM shutdown: ``` java: symbol lookup error: /tmp/javet/2552/libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64.v.5.0.3.so: undefined symbol: exp2 ``` The symbols were missing the whole time — they were simply never called before that point. ## Affected versions v5.0.0 through at least v5.0.3, V8 mode, Linux. Node mode is not affected. | Artifact | `NEEDED` | Unresolved math symbols | |---|---|---| | `libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64` 4.1.7 | `libm.so.6`, `libc.so.6` | 0 | | `libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64` 5.0.0 | `librt.so.1`, `libc.so.6` | 12 | | `libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64` 5.0.3 | `librt.so.1`, `libc.so.6` | 12 | `linux-arm64` was not measured, but it is produced by the same CMake branch and is expected to be affected identically. title: Unable to share sgf via gmail when file name contains # character
body_excerpt: I save my games in the format <player> <date> <outcome>. If I play the same persons twice in one night, I usually just add "#2" after the date. I sometimes email the record to the other player, but last week, I had one record that contained "#2" in the file name, and I ended up having to share it externally. I just reproduced it on my phone (Nexus 6P Android 7.1.1), and it said, "Unable to attach empty file." Attempting to send the actual game record from my tablet running Android 4.4.4 tries to attach a file with the file name of everything up to the # character, e.g., "game #2.sgf" becomes "game ", so sending it fails because the file doesn't exist. Uploading to Google Drive also fails with only the message that it was unsuccessful.

title: The SDK does not handle the deeplinks associated with a campaign in some cases.
body_excerpt: Hi, we have problems with some users that after opening a push sent from the batch dashboard is not directed to the target screen. simply the app opens but does not redirect to the target. Our development and QA teams have tested with exactly the same campaign and with exactly the same deeplink and app opens on the target screen without any problems. We have debugged the problem together with an affected user and what seems to happen is that the deeplink is not managed and propagated by the batch SDK. The activity that is associated in the manifest to manage the deeplinks is not invoked, so the onNewIntent() method is not invoked either. ## Reproduction steps 1. Send a campaign from the batch console with a deeplink pointing to the app schema. 2. Click on the push notification that is generated in the device. 3. The application opens but does not direct to the deeplink target instead it remains on the home screen. NOTE: Only occurs with some users in this condition, Our team is not able to reproduce it. Any idea why the SDK is ignoring the deeplink associated with the campaign in these cases? Thanks in advance. ## Specifications ### SDK Version v2.0.3 ### Installation method Google Play
note: Loose scope: the flow is tapping a push notification and landing on a target screen in the app, so it counts as gui.
